title: Selection leaves a hub, and selected spaces glue into knot spaces
claim: Selection leaves a hub, and selected spaces glue into knot spaces. (1) In every knot space (a connected cubic triple system with a signing on which the knot fails; every such failure is global), removing a line L leaves solutions in which L's three points carry one value up to L's signs: exactly the two complementary all-equal patterns. The leftover is a hub, and the space minus L, with ports L, is the point side of a 3-edge cut. (2) Splicing a knot space at a line into another at a point (each point of the line joined to one line through the point) gives a knot space for exactly one switching class of signs on the three new incidences (two of the eight choices). (3) Both contractions of a simple 3-edge cut of a knot space (three distinct ports and slot lines) are knot spaces, the point side closed by a line and the line side closed by a point; so every simple cut is a splice of selected spaces along a leftover hub. (4) With THREEFOLD-GRAMMAR, every knot space is assembled by splices from Fano atoms and planar glue (whose pieces may repeat an incidence, the non-simple cuts), with 4-sums for non-planar glue. Checked on the 8 census knot spaces, on all 1216 splices of pairs of census knot spaces up to 13 points at every line and point, and on all nontrivial 3-edge cuts of the census spaces and of their splices up to 10 points.
failure_conditions: A knot space in which removing a line leaves its points with more than two patterns, or untied.
A splice of two knot spaces that fails for no sign choice of the new incidences.
A nontrivial 3-edge cut of a knot space with a contraction that is not a knot space.
foundation_claim_scope: Signed knot systems on connected cubic triple systems; splices along 3-edge cuts.
